hook: The sailor who crossed the Atlantic in 1492, thinking he had reached Asia.

pages.x: Christopher Columbus was born in Genoa in 1451, son of a wool weaver. He went to sea young, survived a shipwreck off Portugal by clinging to an oar and swimming ashore, and settled in Lisbon, making maps and sailing as far as West Africa.

He believed he could reach Asia by sailing west. Experts agreed the Earth was round, but said he had badly underestimated its size, which he had. Portugal and others turned him down. In 1492, after six years of asking, Spain's monarchs said yes.
pages.cap: Queen Isabella, who paid for the voyage

pages.x: On 3 August 1492 he sailed from Palos with three ships, the Santa María, the Pinta and the Niña, and about 90 men. After five weeks out of sight of land the crew was close to mutiny. Then, on 12 October, a lookout shouted "Land!": an island in the Bahamas.

Sure he had reached Asia, he called the people he met, the Taíno, "Indians". He wrote that they were gentle and generous, and in the same letter that they would make good servants. On Christmas Day, off Hispaniola, the Santa María ran aground.

He made three more voyages and became governor of Hispaniola. He ruled so harshly that in 1500 he was arrested and shipped home in chains. The Taíno were forced to dig for gold, and within decades most had died from cruelty and European diseases.

Stranded on Jamaica in 1504, with the islanders refusing to bring more food, he used an almanac to predict an eclipse of the Moon. He warned them that God would take away the Moon unless they helped. When it darkened, they came running with food.

Columbus died in 1506 still believing he had reached Asia. His voyages linked Europe and the Americas for good, bringing new foods and riches, and also conquest, slavery and the deaths of millions of Native Americans.
pts: Began the lasting link between Europe and the Americas
His arrival brought conquest and catastrophe to Native peoples
